newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Fogade to lower bank insurance.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Fogade to lower bank insurance.

text.p: Venezuelan Deposits Guarantee Fund Fogade is considering ways to reduce the amount local banks have to pay to guarantee deposits, Fogade president Esther de Margulis said.

Venezuelan banks currently pay two percent of the value of their deposits to Fogade. Margulis said those rates would be lowered to 1.5 percent by July, then to 1.0 percent by the end of the year, and finally to 0.5 percent in 1998.
"First, however, we have to sort out Fogade's debts with the Central Bank," Margulis said. "I hope that will be done before June," she added, without giving details.

Fogade owes the Central Bank 1.4 trillion bolivars ($3 billion) for bailouts the Central Bank provided in Venezuela's 1994-5 financial crisis. Before the crisis, Fogade required a 0.5 deposits insurance rate from Venezuelan banks.

Local bankers have long complained that the two percent deposit rate, raised during the financial crisis, increased their operating costs. Fogade said they were reducing the rate in light of the recovery of the financial sector.
